source_title: The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance — Season 1 Episode 1 opening witness
continuity_scope: Netflix’s The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance prequel-series continuity only, restricted to Season 1 Episode 1, “End. Begin. All the Same.” Netflix’s official episode synopsis supplies the secret/guard/Skeksis/Crystal premise; the primary episode supplies the three named young Gelfling who are dramatically agentive in that witness; Jim Henson Company material establishes the television-series/prequel boundary and three-Gelfling framing. The 1982 film, novels, comics, games, and later episodes are excluded.

coverage_rule: Include only named individual puppet characters who are dramatically agentive in the selected episode-one witness and belong to the official three-young-Gelfling framing: Rian, Brea, and Deet. The young guard’s publicly described discovery is identified with Rian only through the primary episode. Gelfling, Skeksis, Mystics, clans, Darkening/essence concepts, artifacts, places, institutions, and prophecy remain terms or omissions. Individually named Skeksis, family figures, other credited puppets, and unnamed groups are omitted because the selected official episode synopsis does not establish claim-specific individual records for them.
omissions: All individual named or unnamed figures outside the declared three-character episode-one cohort, including individual Skeksis, Mystics, family members, guards, servants, and other credited puppets.
The 1982 The Dark Crystal feature-film continuity; novels, comics, games, board-game material, companion books, documentaries, bonus material, and all later Age of Resistance episodes.

Clans, peoples, species, the Darkening, essence-extraction mechanics, institutions, prophecies, artifacts, creature anatomy, places beyond Thra and the Crystal of Truth, and complete social/cosmological systems as character nodes.

Specific death, injury, bodily process, body-horror, oppression, environmental causality, age/youth, disability/body, race/ethnicity/cultural coding, romance, gender, performer/voice identity, puppetry technique, and later-reveal claims not directly supported by the selected official synopsis or primary episode scene.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, non-official recaps, social posts, unlicensed transcripts, and book/comic lore extrapolation.
uncertainties: Netflix’s Episode 1 synopsis says a young guard discovers a terrible secret about Skeksis overlords and their powerful Crystal of Truth. It does not name the guard or explain the secret. Rian is identified only from the primary on-screen episode; no further mechanics, source, victim, or outcome is stated here.

Jim Henson Company material says three young Gelfling discover the secret and begin a rebellion-oriented journey, but does not name them in the cited logline. Brea and Deet are therefore included only as named, agentive Episode 1 figures; no later quest event is assigned.

Gelfling and Skeksis are fictional peoples/groups, not real-world race, ethnicity, culture, disability, body type, or moral categories. The account neither turns puppet construction into character ontology nor conflates a performer with a character.

The series uses ecological and oppression-related framing in broad promotional text, but the selected Episode 1 synopsis supports only overlord control, a secret, a Crystal, and the later-series logline’s life-draining premise. It is not used to diagnose real-world trauma, oppression, environmental systems, or physical harm.
Age of Resistance is officially a prequel made many years before the 1982 film. This relationship marks separation, not permission to import film facts or anticipate later outcomes.
evidence_basis: Official Netflix and Jim Henson Company materials, plus the selected Netflix episode as primary audiovisual evidence for name-to-scene identification. Netflix supplies the precise Episode 1 synopsis; Henson supplies the series/prequel boundary and three-Gelfling premise. No fan source or later episode is used as canonical evidence.
